 Order
This petition under Section 439 (2) of Cr.P.C. has been filed for cancellation of bail granted to respondent No. 2 vide order dated 09.12.2021 by this Court in MCRC No. 58794 of 2021.

2. As per prosecution story, on 26.3.2021, complainant lodged a written complaint at the police station to the effect that respondent No. 2 / accused took loan of Rs.27,00,000/- from him for establishing a beauty parlor and petrol pump, however, he did not return the money even after four years.

Upon this, FIR bearing Crime No. 201/2021 was registered against respondent No. 2 /
accused for offence under Sections 420 and 406 of IPC and during the course of investigation,
respondent No. 2 was arrested.

Respondent No. 2 filed various bail applications and fifth bail application NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:22040 2 MCRC-52024-2023 was allowed vide order impugned by this Court for cancellation of which present petition has been filed.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner argued that respondent No. 2 was granted bail vide order impugned in the light of the submission made on behalf of respondent No. 2 that "parties are arrived at compromise and copy of compromise agreement has been filed along with list of documents", however, after grant of bail, cheques mentioned in the Anubandh Patra (agreement)
dated 08.12.2021 got dishonored which shows that with malafide intention, agreement was executed Pankaj Mittal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152218162/
1 by father of respondent No. 2.

sentences.text: Under these circumstances, since the bail was obtained by respondent No. 2 by misleading the court, therefore, the same deserves to be cancelled.

Hence, prayed to recall /
cancel the bail granted to the respondent No. 2.
4.

On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No. 2 vehemently opposed the petition and argued that at the time of argument in the bail application, matter was compromise by the parties by execution of an agreement between the father of respondent No. 2 with petitioner / complainant Pankaj.
Therefore, it cannot be said that there was misleading of fact.
It is further argued that the bail was granted with certain conditions and petitioner has failed to show that respondent No. 2 has breached an condition of the bail order.

The order-sheets filed by respondent No. 2 also indicate that petitioner avoided recording of his evidence for a long period of time and only recently, his statement has been recorded, therefore, there is no delay in the trial on the part of respondent No. 2.

Further argument is that it is a trite law that the bail order cannot be cancelled for violation of terms of a NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:22040 3 MCRC-52024-2023 compromise on the basis of which the bail was granted.
In support of his arguments, learned counsel for respondent No.2 relied upon the case law of Biman Chatterjee vs. Sanchita Chatterjee & Anr.; AIR 2004 SC 1699 and prayed to dismiss the petition.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
5. Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the available record.
6.

The Supreme Court in the case of Himanshu Sharma vs. State of Madhya Pradesh; Criminal Appeals arising out of SlP (Criminal) No(s). 786 of 2024 and 2032 of 2024, decided on 20.2.2024,
laid down circumstances for cancellation of bail which are mentioned below:-
"Generally the grounds for cancellation of bail, broadly, are, (i) the accused misuses his liberty by indulging in similar criminal activity, (ii) interferes with the course of investigation, (iii) attempts to tamper with evidence or witnesses, (iv) threatens witnesses or indulges in similar activities which would hamper smooth investigation,
(v) there is likelihood of his fleeing to another country, (vi) attempts to make himself scarce by going underground or becoming unavailable to the investigating agency,
(vii) attempts to place himself beyond the reach of his surety, etc.

entities.text: Himanshu Sharma vs. State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
These grounds are illustrative and not exhaustive."
7.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in case the case of Dolat Ram Vs. State of Haryana [(1995) 1 SCC 349 : 1995 SCC (Cri) 237] has held as under:
"Very cogent and overwhelming circumstances are necessary for an order directing the cancellation of the bail, already granted.

entities.text: Dolat Ram Vs. State of Haryana [(1995) 1 SCC 349 : 1995 SCC (Cri) 237]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Generally speaking, the grounds for cancellation of bail, broadly (illustrative and not exhaustive) are: interference or attempt to interfere NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:22040 4 MCRC-52024-2023 with the due course of administration of Justice or evasion or attempt to evade the due course of justice or abuse of the concession granted to the accused in any manner.

The satisfaction of the court, on the basis of material placed on the record of the possibility of the accused absconding is yet another reason Pankaj Mittal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152218162/
2 justifying the cancellation of bail.

entities.text: Pankaj Mittal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, bail once granted should not be cancelled in a mechanical manner without considering whether any supervening circumstances have rendered it no longer conducive to a fair trial to allow the accused to retain his freedom by enjoying the concession of bail during the trial.

These principles, it appears, were lost sight of by the High Court when it decided to cancel the bail,
already granted.

The High Court it appears to us overlooked the distinction of the factors relevant for rejecting bail in a non-bailable case in the first instance and the cancellation of bail already granted"
8.

The perusal of record indicates that at the time of hearing of bail application, document i.e.
agreement was executed by father of respondent No. 2 with petitioner Pankaj Mittal, therefore, it cannot be said that there was no compromise at the time of passing of the bail order dated 09.12.2021.
Impugned bail order also indicates that bail was granted to respondent No. 2 with certain conditions and there is nothing on record to indicate that respondent No. 2 has violated those conditions.

9. The Supreme Court in the case of Biman Chatterjee (supra) has held that "Though in the original order granting bail there is a reference to an agreement of the parties to have a talk of compromise through the media of well wishers, there is no submission made to the court that there will be a compromise or that the appellant would take back his wife.

Be that as it may, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:22040 5 MCRC-52024-2023 in our opinion, the courts below could not have cancelled the bail solely on the ground that the appellant had failed to keep up his promise made to the court.

Here we hasten to observe first of all from the material on record, we do not find that there was any compromise arrived at between the parties at all, hence, question of fulfilling the terms of such compromise does not arise.
That apart non-fulfilment of the terms of the compromise cannot be the basis of granting or cancelling a bail.

The grant of bail under the Criminal Procedure Code is governed by the provision of Chapter XXXIII of the Code and the provision therein does not contemplate either granting of a bail on the basis of an assurance of a compromise or cancellation of a bail for violation of the terms of such compromise.
What the court has to bear in mind while granting bail is what is provided for in Section 437 of the said Code.

In our opinion, having granted the bail under the said provision of law, it is not open to the trial court or the High Court to cancel the same on a ground alien to the grounds mentioned for cancellation of bail in the said provision of law".
10.

It is also well settled that very cogent and overwhelming circumstances or grounds are required to cancel the bail already granted and unless a strong case based on any supervening event is made out, an order granting bail is not to be lightly interfered with under Section 439 (2) CrPC.
11.
In this case, learned counsel for the petitioner has failed to show any cogent, overwhelming circumstances or ground.
Under these circumstances, there is no reason to recall the order granting bail to the respondent No. 2 / accused.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:22040 6 MCRC-52024-2023 Pankaj Mittal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 December, 2024

2 vide impugned order, sans merit and is hereby dismissed.
